item.title: Gloss 0.1.2
item.description:
Fixes for the first round of reports from 0.1.1, plus a few new things.

Fixed

  • Drafts only leave Gloss when you press Send. The Claude Code and Codex prompt hook could hand every draft in a folder to the agent, unseen, whenever a prompt was submitted (including the prompt a send itself submits) and mark them sent. The hook is gone. After updating, open Settings › Agents and press Update on Claude Code and Codex to remove it from their settings (a backup is kept). Agents now only see notes you've sent them, and Copy as Packet leaves notes as drafts.
  • Notes keep their place when files change. When a note's text appears in several places, Gloss picks the one whose surrounding lines match, and flags the note for a look when it can't be sure. A file changed while it was closed has its notes found again when it opens. A sent note that loses its text and finds it again stays sent; a resolved note stays resolved.
  • The notes filter bar no longer wraps when the panel is narrow: it drops the title, then the counts.

New

  • Back and Forward through the documents you've viewed, across folders and hosts: Go › Back (⌃⌘←) and Forward (⌃⌘→), or the chevrons in the toolbar.
  • Agents can show you things. Over MCP an agent can ask you a question beside the lines it's about (it waits under Attention; reply and send to answer), open a file at a range of lines, and add a project folder to your favorites.
  • Images in Jira issues and Confluence pages show inline, and attached images and PDFs open in their viewers so you can note a region of them.
  • Paths from notes to cards are smoother and move exactly with the page.

item.title: Gloss 0.1.1
item.description:
First release of Gloss.

  • Browse folders on this Mac and over ssh, and annotate any region of any file
  • Send notes to Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
  • Review pull requests, Jira issues and Confluence pages
  • Updates and in-app feedback
